title: Introduction to Epidemiology and Sources of Data

questions.stem: Which question is typical of epidemiology rather than clinical medicine?

options.A: What is the leading cause of death in this population?
options.C: What dose should this child receive?

questions.explanation: Epidemiology studies populations; clinical medicine focuses on individuals. B, C, D, E: These are individual clinical questions.
questions.source: Introduction to Epidemiology and Sources of Data, slide 8

questions.stem: Investigating 27 students with vomiting and diarrhea, you first chart cases by time of onset, the event attended, and age and sex. Which type of epidemiology is this?
questions.explanation: Describing frequency and pattern by time, place, and person (when, where, who) is descriptive epidemiology. A: Analytical epidemiology asks why: it tests determinants. B: Clinical epidemiology links epidemiology to patient care. C: Surveillance is ongoing, systematic collection of health data, not the description of one outbreak. D: Evaluation assesses interventions after they are implemented.
questions.source: Introduction to Epidemiology and Sources of Data, slides 3, 11–12

questions.stem: Influenza cases in a city rise well above the usual seasonal level for that time and place. This is best termed:
questions.explanation: An epidemic (outbreak) is an increase in cases above what is normally expected for that place and time. A: Endemic is the constant baseline presence. B: Sporadic means scattered, irregular cases. C: A pandemic crosses international boundaries. E: Epidemiologic transition is a long-term shift from infectious to chronic disease patterns.
questions.source: Introduction to Epidemiology and Sources of Data, slide 28

questions.stem: Which contribution belongs to John Snow?

options.A: Quantified patterns of birth and death in London's population
options.B: Linked cholera deaths to contaminated water by comparing water sources
options.C: Inoculated a boy with cowpox to protect against smallpox
options.D: Identified cardiovascular risk factors in a prospective cohort
options.E: Analyzed British mortality by marital status and occupation

questions.explanation: Snow (1854) compared cholera deaths by water company and linked cases to the Broad Street pump: father of field epidemiology. A: John Graunt (17th century). C: Edward Jenner (1796). D: Framingham Heart Study (1948). E: William Farr (19th century).
questions.source: Introduction to Epidemiology and Sources of Data, slides 18, 21–22, 24

questions.stem: Lebanon maintains a database that collects information on every person diagnosed with cancer. This source of health data is a:
questions.explanation: A registry is a database of cases diagnosed with a particular disease (e.g., Lebanon's cancer registry). A: A census enumerates the whole population with demographic data (Lebanon's last: 1932). B: Surveillance is ongoing collection, analysis and dissemination of data on health events to detect outbreaks and monitor burden. D: Death certificates record causes of death (ICD-11). E: Discharge summaries record hospitalizations.
questions.source: Introduction to Epidemiology and Sources of Data, slides 29–31

questions.stem: In the same outbreak, investigators compare how often students who ate the chicken salad became ill with how often those who didn't eat it became ill. This step is:
questions.explanation: Comparing groups to identify a determinant (why it happened) is analytical epidemiology. A: Descriptive epidemiology describes time, place and person without testing causes. B: Surveillance is ongoing routine data collection. C: Clinical medicine diagnoses and treats individuals. D: Epidemiologic transition is a long-term change in disease patterns.
questions.source: Introduction to Epidemiology and Sources of Data, slides 11–12, 15
